Visioner BIG | 🇵🇱 🇺🇦 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Poland is preparing to tighten airspace restrictions along its border with Ukraine to support military operations, following a series of reported Russian drone and missile incursions that have raised concerns about security on NATO’s eastern flank. Polish Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk said the proposed restricted zone would extend from more than 10 kilometers to several dozen kilometers from the Ukrainian border. The measures could take effect in late December or early January. Poland already restricts daytime flights below approximately three kilometers in the border area, while nighttime flights are generally prohibited, with exceptions for emergencies. The announcement follows reports that a drone entered Polish airspace on November 24 without being intercepted despite authorization to engage it. A day earlier, debris reportedly linked to three Russian missiles was discovered in the Lublin and Podkarpackie regions. The proposed restrictions would give Polish forces greater control over airspace near Ukraine and could help them respond more quickly to unidentified aerial threats. The recent incidents highlight the difficulty of protecting NATO territory from drones and missiles operating close to the border. Warsaw’s measures reflect growing concern that Russia’s attacks on Ukraine could create further security risks for neighboring alliance members. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet
